title: State Highways
description: The first digits of Hawaii state highways are nicely grouped by island. However, there is not much organization past that

title: Hawaii Island vegetation
description: Hawaii Island is characterized by dense vegetation, lots of ferns, and a jungle/rainforest vibe

title: City of Hilo
description: Hilo is very lush and green, often with a grid that is easy to line up. Mauna Kea can often be seen to the west

title: Volcanic rocks
description: Hawaii island has the only currently active volcano of the archipel and is the most recent formed island, so lots of volcanix rock is common

title: Mountains of Hawaii island
description: The big island has large, sloping mountains, such as Mauna Loa and Mauna Kea

title: Kona area
description: A weirdly good meta for the west side of big island is roads taht are angled SE-NW

title: Hualalai mountain
description: Hualalai (a large mountainà rises to the east of Kona

title: Central areas of Hawaii
description: Central areas of hawaii will have mountains all around

title: North east of Hawaii island
description: The north east coast is characterized by planted eucalyptus overlooking the ocean

title: Mauna Loa observatory road
description: The of road of Mauna Loa observatory looks like Mars, and is poor quality

title: Maui street signs
description: Maui has street signs with "long arrow" tabs and blank tabs

title: Central Maui landscape
description: Central Maui has the very recognizable "west Maui mountains" to the west and Haleakala to the east

title: West Maui landscape
description: The West Maui landscape is recongnizable with Molokai and/or Lanai often to the west, and the west Maui mountains rising to the east

title: Hana Highway
description: The Hana Highway runs along the east cost of Maui and is often narrow and lush

title: Haleakala
description: Haleakala is the tallest point on Maui and the road up can be above the clouds in a rocky landscaoes

title: Molokai landscape
description: Molokai has red soil and is very dry

title: East Molokai
description: East Molokai has mountains to the north and a road that gets gradually narrower

title: West Molokai landscape
description: West Molokai has a very distinctive landscape

title: Honolulu landscape
description: Honolulu has many skyscrappers and hootels

title: Honolulu valleys
description: Honolulu has a lot of narrow valleys bordered by ridges the the east into the Koolau Mountains

title: East Oahu landscape
description: East Oahu has very distinct ridged mountains rising to the west

title: Wainae mountains
description: Central Oahu often has the Waianae mountains visible far away to the west

title: Central Oahu landscape
description: Central Oahu has a lot of red soil and red roads, ans is also very agricultural

title: West Oahu valleys
description: West Oahu has deep valleys sourrounded by ridged mountains, these are drier than the east Oahu mountains and with fewer trees

title: Kapolei and Eva landscape
description: The Waianae mountains are often visible to ther north in Kapoloei and Ewa

title: Kauai mountains
description: The Kaui mountains are smaller and more craggy than the mountains on other Hawaiian islands

title: Kauai red dirt
description: Kaui has often red dirt, not as dry as Molokai and Lanai

title: Kauai north landscape
description: Kauai north is very lush with reddish roads and mountains to the west and south

title: Lanai cook pines
description: Lanai, especially Lanai City has red soil and lots of Cook Pines

title: Lanai mountain rang
description: This mountain range os to the east in most locations

title: Keomuku Highway
description: Maui and Molokai visible to the north on Keomuku Highway in the north east

title: Kahoolawe dark red soil
description: Kahoolawe have dark red soil

title: Kahoolawe "urban"
description: On Kahoolawe, buildings and people can only be found in the south west near Hanakanae beach

title: Grid neighbourhoods
description: There are a few very distinctive neighbourhoods on the main island, with their characteristic grids, forming the Ocean View and Paradise Park neighbourhoods

title: Oklahoma fence
description: Red metallic fences are very common in Oklahoma and the surrounding states, particularly Kansas, Texas, and Arkansas. Not 100% reliable, so look for other clues before sending. (★★★)

title: Texas little bumps
description: These little rectangular bumps on center lines are unique to Texas. Round bumps exist in some other states, but rectangular ones are only seen in Texas. (★★★)

title: Massachusetts pole plates
description: These rectangular plates, which can be white or yellow, can be seen on the side of poles in eastern Massachusetts, Rhode Island and Connecticut. Very rarely seen elsewhere. (★★)

title: Alabama pole plate
description: Fine plates with a round part on the side, seen on most poles in Alabama. The author has never seen anything like this elsewhere. (★★)

title: Ohio gap
description: In Ohio, you can often see gaps in road lines where there is a raised pavement marker (RPM). Also sometimes seen in Tennessee or New Jersey, but much rarer. (★★)

title: South Carolina roads
description: In South Carolina, small roads will often have no road lines, with southern RPMs in the middle — almost only seen in SC. Elsewhere RPMs are always next to road lines, though those can sometimes be faded, so be careful. (★)

title: Oregon white lines
description: Short, fine lines often seen in between Oregon's road lines, which are usually wide. Similar lines exist elsewhere, but this is useful to distinguish Oregon from surrounding states, especially Washington, which also often uses wide road lines. (★)

title: Kentucky roads
description: In Kentucky it is pretty common to see roads with no middle line and only white outer lines. Also common in California (already covered on Plonk It). (★)

title: Yellow post
description: Yellow posts like this one are common in Colorado, seen more rarely in Utah or Texas, and rarely elsewhere. (★)

title: Oregon bollard
description: This bollard is extremely common in Oregon and almost exclusive to this state. Rarely seen in California, and even then usually not exactly the same (bigger white rectangle, or not all the way on top). (★★★)

title: Utah bollard
description: This bollard is unique to Utah. (★★)

title: Utah and Idaho bollard
description: This bollard, with a white square on top, is unique to Utah, Idaho and Arizona. In Arizona there is only one screw, whereas in Utah there are two. If the square is not totally on top, it should be Idaho. (★★)

title: Green bollards
description: Green bollards are common and almost unique to Idaho and Colorado; they exist in several different forms, not only the one pictured. (★★)

title: Montana yellow rectangular bollard
description: In the western US, this bollard can only be seen in Montana. (★)

title: Idaho rectangular bollard
description: These bollards with a rectangle on top are common in Idaho and, in the western US, can only be seen there. The rectangle can be white or yellow and is smaller than the one on the Utah/Idaho bollard. (★)

title: Round bollard with circle on top
description: This bollard with a white circle totally on top can be found in Illinois, Iowa, Nebraska and New Mexico — part of the wider round-bollard family also seen in Wyoming, Colorado and Oklahoma. Do not confuse it with the bollard whose circle is not totally on top; rarely seen elsewhere. (★)

title: Round bollard with circle not totally on top
description: This bollard, with a white circle not totally on top, can only be seen in Wyoming and Colorado. Be careful not to mistake it for the bollard with the circle fully on top. (★★★)

title: Round Wyoming bollard
description: A round bollard with the top of the post painted white means you are in Wyoming — though not all round bollards in Wyoming look like this. (★★★)

title: Green post
description: Round bollards with a green-painted post are common in Colorado and can also be seen in New Mexico. (★)

title: Bollard with double circle on top
description: This bollard, with 2 circles on each side, is unique to western Nebraska, New Mexico and Illinois. (★)

title: Bollard with 3 circles spaced
description: This bollard, with space between its circles, is common in New Mexico and Colorado, and can more rarely be seen in Wyoming. (★★)

title: Bollard with 3 circles close together
description: This bollard, with circles very close to each other, is common in Oklahoma and can rarely be seen in Texas and New Mexico. Do not mistake it for the spaced-circle bollard. (★)

title: Utah pole plate
description: Most poles in Utah, south-east Idaho and Wyoming have a rectangular yellow plate like this one. Be very careful, as similar plates can also be seen in Oregon, California and Washington. (★)

title: North Carolina white lines
description: It is common to see white lines in between road lines in North Carolina, which also has fairly wide road lines. Use with a lot of caution: such white lines can be seen pretty much anywhere. (★)

title: Yellow wide rectangular bollard
description: This lower-than-usual bollard is very common in South Dakota and Nebraska, and fairly common in Louisiana and Texas. Can also be seen in pretty much any state, but more rarely. (★)

title: Arizona round white marks
description: On some roads in Arizona you can see this white circle with a dot in it. Such markings are very rare elsewhere, and the author has never seen them in any state that resembles Arizona. (★)

title: Red roads
description: Roads with a red tint are particularly common in Nebraska and South Dakota, and more rarely Minnesota. Such roads can be seen anywhere, so be careful. (★)

title: North Dakota pole top
description: This pole top is very common in North Dakota, and can also be seen in Iowa, Minnesota and South Dakota. Be careful not to mix it up with other similar pole tops. (★)

title: Kansas rumble strips
description: In Kansas, almost every outer rumble strip is small, consisting of 5 to 12 rumbles, unlike other states which use much longer rumble strips. Also true on interstate highways in South Dakota (I-90 and I-29 through the state), and in other states sometimes. (★)
